lessons.title: Train Test Split
lessons.description: Finish train_test_split(xs, ratio) so it returns (train, test). The train list is the first floor(len(xs) * ratio) items. The test list is the rest. The test checks that train_test_split([1, 2, 3, 4, 5], 0.6) equals ([1, 2, 3], [4, 5]).
learning_objectives: Depot potters recount crates before dawn, and split data into train and test.

tests.name: test_split
tests.unittest_code:
def test_split(self):
    tr, te = train_test_split([1, 2, 3, 4, 5], 0.6)
    self.assertEqual(tr, [1, 2, 3])
    self.assertEqual(te, [4, 5])

lessons.title: Practice Deterministic Shuffle Split
lessons.description: Implement shuffle_split(xs, ratio, seed) using random.Random(seed).shuffle on a copy. The test checks that len(tr) equals 2; len(te) equals 2; sorted(tr + te) equals [1, 2, 3, 4].
learning_objectives: Ridge potters recount crates before dawn, and shuffle before splitting.
lessons.starter_code:
import random

def shuffle_split(xs, ratio, seed):
    # TODO
    pass
lessons.solution_code:
import random

def shuffle_split(xs, ratio, seed):
    items = list(xs)
    random.Random(seed).shuffle(items)
    n = int(len(items) * ratio)
    return items[:n], items[n:]

tests.name: test_shuffle_split
tests.unittest_code:
def test_shuffle_split(self):
    tr, te = shuffle_split([1, 2, 3, 4], 0.5, 0)
    self.assertEqual(len(tr), 2)
    self.assertEqual(len(te), 2)
    self.assertEqual(sorted(tr + te), [1, 2, 3, 4])

source.name: Python official documentation (docs.python.org) — random — 'Shuffle the sequence x in place.'
